成人长新冠(新型冠状病毒感染后期综合征)中有监督运动对免疫学效应的影响:一项随机交叉试验的二次分析
item.description: 摘要 长新冠(新型冠状病毒感染后期综合征)影响约5%–30%的感染幸存者,其特征为持续性疲劳、呼吸困难、运动不耐受及认知障碍。我们评估了成人长新冠患者在有监督运动下的免疫学效应。在EXER-COVID随机2×2交叉试验的预先指定探索性亚研究中,参与者在3–5天清洗期后,先完成为期6周的有监督运动项目(每周两次)或常规护理,随后交叉。通过多重免疫分析法测定血浆细胞因子(IL-1β、IL-6、IL-10、TNF-α、MCP-1/CCL2、MIP-1α/CCL3、MIP-1β/CCL4及IP-10/CXCL10)。免疫表型分析包括20种CD4+和CD8+ T细胞亚群及5种先天免疫细胞群体。治疗效应通过期内变化得分估计,并通过Benjamini–Hochberg程序(假阳性率<5%)进行多重检验校正。校正前,5个变量达到名义显著性(2个CD8+ T细胞亚群及IL-1β、IL-10和MIP-1α),但校正后无一保持显著。未观察到先天免疫细胞群体的变化,亦未检测到携带效应。有监督运动在校正多重比较后与显著免疫学变化无关,支持中等强度运动在PESE阴性成人长新冠患者中的短期免疫学安全性(ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT04797871)。

通过在单一mRNA免疫原中配对发散受体结合域以增强对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的抗原性广度
item.description: 能够诱导广泛中和抗体(bnAbs)的疫苗是疫情防控的重要目标。然而,在疫苗领域,如何有意识地招募识别不同病毒变异株间保守表位的罕见B细胞克隆仍是一大挑战。已知bnAbs通常通过亲和力成熟过程中的大量体细胞超突变产生,而本研究描述了一种bnAb选择的替代机制。我们设计了一种mRNA 疫苗,其中两个抗原性不同的(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2)严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株(Omicron和Delta;O-Δ)的受体结合域(RBD)在单一多肽链上进行物理融合。该设计预计可增强能够同时结合两个RBD上保守表位的B细胞抗原受体的亲和力。匹配的非发散串联RBD(Delta-Delta;Δ-Δ)作为对照。在小鼠中,免疫接种诱导了强效抗体应答并提高了交叉反应性B细胞的频率,这些B细胞可识别Delta、Omicron及2002年大流行株SARS-CoV的RBD。通过多色RBD四聚体和单细胞B细胞受体测序,我们证明了广度的产生通过两种不同途径实现。发散的疫苗优先富集克隆上不同的交叉反应性B细胞(不存在于非交叉反应性B细胞库中),其体细胞超突变水平较低,与胚系偏向前体的选择一致。相比之下,匹配的对照疫苗主要在现有克隆系内产生交叉反应性(交叉反应性与非交叉反应性细胞间存在克隆重叠),且突变负担更高,与亲和力成熟驱动的广度获取一致。本研究建立了一种简单的模块化抗原设计原理,即在单一支架上并置适当发散的抗原可促进bnAb倾向B细胞的富集。

item.title: 喜马偕尔邦(印度)严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2奥密克戎谱系新兴亚分支的分子流行病学:一项横断面研究
item.description: 引言:严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2)表现出持续的遗传变异,导致全球范围内出现多种病毒谱系。这些变异株可能影响病毒的传播能力、致病潜力和免疫逃逸,从而改变疾病模式。基因组监测(基因组监测)允许系统追踪病毒变异株和流行变种,因此监测对于制定知情的公共卫生计划和临床准备至关重要。目的:检测印度喜马偕尔邦山区奥密克戎谱系变种的出现情况。材料与方法:本横断面研究于2024年1月至6月在印度喜马偕尔邦曼迪的Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri医学院进行。所有来自该州四个病毒研究与诊断实验室(VRDLs)的Ct值≤30的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2阳性样本均被纳入研究。使用Q-Line分子病毒RNA提取试剂盒进行RNA提取,并在牛津纳米孔MinION平台上进行全基因组测序(Whole 基因组 Sequencing,WGS)。使用Medaka和Nanopolish生成共识序列,用于变异株识别和系统发育分析。所有人口统计学和临床数据,包括年龄、性别、临床表现和血清学状态,均使用Microsoft Excel 2021记录并整理。研究聚焦于生成的基因组序列,数据以数字和百分比形式呈现。结果:共收到30例严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2阳性样本。在严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2阳性病例中,成年女性占比最高,为17例(56.7%),其中大多数患者年龄在19-60岁之间,共17例(56.7%),且大多数样本来自Shimla,共11例(36.7%)。研究发现,19例(63.3%)为JN.1亚谱系,是感染的主要原因。大多数病例(20例,66.7%)报告至门诊部门,其中35%(7例)表现出轻度症状,如发热和咳嗽。尽管有23例(76.7%)接种了疫苗,但仍有10例(33.3%)需要住院治疗,且未报告任何关注变异株(关注变异株)。结论:追踪严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株显示,奥密克戎的JN.1亚谱系在本地流行,且临床表现通常较轻。持续的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2遗传变异强调了将基因组监测(基因组监测)与流行病学数据整合的必要性,以实现新兴变异株的早期检测并加强控制策略。研究问题与背景:严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的持续遗传变异推动了新谱系的出现,这些新谱系可能对传播能力、致病性和免疫逃逸产生潜在影响,因此需要监测流行变异株以支持公共卫生规划。本研究旨在检测印度喜马偕尔邦奥密克戎谱系亚变种的出现,填补了该地区基因组监测(基因组监测)方面的空白。研究设计与人群:本横断面研究于2024年1月至6月在印度喜马偕尔邦曼迪的Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri医学院进行。所有来自该州四个病毒研究与诊断实验室(VRDLs)的Ct值≤30的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2阳性样本均被纳入研究。方法:使用Q-Line分子病毒RNA提取试剂盒进行RNA提取,并在牛津纳米孔MinION平台上进行全基因组测序(Whole 基因组 Sequencing,WGS)。使用Medaka和Nanopolish生成共识序列,用于变异株识别和系统发育分析。主要结果:共收到30例严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2阳性样本,其中成年女性占56.7%(17/30),大多数患者年龄在19-60岁之间(56.7%,17/30)。样本主要来自Shimla(36.7%,11/30),其中63.3%(19/30)的病例被鉴定为JN.1亚谱系。大多数病例(66.7%,20/30)报告至门诊部门,其中35%(7/20)表现出轻度症状,如发热和咳嗽。尽管有76.7%(23/30)的病例接种了疫苗,但仍有33.3%(10/30)需要住院治疗,且未报告任何关注变异株(关注变异株)。解释与创新性:在测序病例中,JN.1亚谱系的主导地位表明奥密克戎亚变种在本地持续传播,且临床表现通常较轻。本研究强调了基因组监测(基因组监测)在区域环境下检测新兴变异株的实用性。科学与公共卫生意义:这些发现支持将基因组监测(基因组监测)与流行病学数据整合,以实现新兴严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株的早期检测,并加强山区地区的本地控制策略。JN.1亚谱系的主导地位突显了需要针对性的公共卫生应对措施。局限性与证据强度:由于样本量较小(n=30)和单中心设计,研究结果的推广性受到限制,且依赖Ct值≤30可能引入选择偏倚。由于横断面研究设计和缺乏对混杂因素的控制,证据强度中等。

COVID-19 dashboard
item.description: The WHO COVID-19 dashboard provides a global summary of confirmed SARS-CoV-2 cases and deaths, with data collected from countries, territories, and areas. It includes information on case definitions, testing strategies, and reporting practices, which vary by region. The dashboard has been updated since March 2020, with weekly data from July 2023 onwards. Data is subject to continuous verification and may change due to retrospective updates or shifts in reporting standards. WHO acknowledges that case detection, testing, and reporting practices differ globally, which can lead to under or overestimation of true case and death counts. Additionally, some countries have stopped reporting or changed their reporting frequency, which may affect the completeness of the data. The dashboard serves as a tool for monitoring the pandemic's spread and impact, but it is important to note that the data reflects official reports and may not capture all cases or deaths accurately.

item.title: 呼吸道病毒活动水平 - 美国疾病控制与预防中心 | CDC (.gov)
item.description: 美国疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)于2026年8月28日发布了一份报告,详细介绍了呼吸道病毒活动水平及相关公共卫生更新。该报告包含与大肠杆菌和沙门氏菌相关的暴发的信息,以及埃博拉和环孢子虫病的最新情况。然而,该报告并未重点关注严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2,也未提供任何特定暴发的具体病例数、死亡人数或暴露人数。相反,它作为公共卫生主题的总体概述,强调了CDC在监测和应对各类健康威胁方面的作用。该报告未详细说明任何提及的暴发的具体应对措施或控制措施,表明其目的在于提供更广泛的信息概述,而非针对特定严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2活动的专项分析。

item.title: IVAC Researchers Inform Global Guidance on COVID-19 Vaccines - Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health
item.description: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health's International Vaccine Access Center (IVAC) researchers contributed to the World Health Organization's (WHO) first-ever position paper on COVID-19 vaccines, released in 2026. The paper summarizes essential background information on the disease and vaccine performance, offering data-backed recommendations for national immunization programs. The research, funded by the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), evaluated over 5,000 studies assessing vaccine effectiveness across diverse populations, including older adults, immunocompromised individuals, children, and pregnant individuals. The findings indicate that the vaccine remains highly effective at preventing hospitalizations and deaths, with no identified group where it does not work. The paper emphasizes routine vaccination for high-risk populations and suggests that countries may consider it for others based on context-specific factors such as cost-effectiveness. The recommendations are supported by systematic reviews of global evidence and are available in an interactive database for public health decision-makers.

item.title: COVID-19 - Britannica
item.description: The article from Britannica, published on August 25, 2026, provides an overview of SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic. It confirms that the virus was first detected in Wuhan, China, in 2019 and has since spread globally, causing millions of deaths. The disease is primarily transmitted through respiratory droplets and contaminated surfaces, with higher risk for older adults and individuals with chronic illnesses. The article highlights the impact of the pandemic on society, including the shift to remote work and education, and discusses the use of vaccines, antiviral drugs, and other preventive measures to mitigate the spread and severity of the disease. The response includes public health strategies such as social distancing, surface disinfection, and face mask usage, as well as the development of vaccines and therapeutic monoclonal antibodies. The article does not provide specific details on the current status of the pandemic but emphasizes the ongoing efforts to manage its effects.

item.title: The Lasting Effects of COVID-19 on Kids - Children's Hospital Association
item.description: The Children's Hospital Association published a news article on August 27, 2026, discussing the long-term effects of COVID-19 on children. The article highlights the findings of the Pediatric COVID Outcomes Study (PECOS), a collaboration between Children's National Hospital and the National Institutes of Health, which enrolled over 1,000 children and adolescents. The study identified persistent symptoms such as fatigue, headaches, and cognitive difficulties in some children, with variations by age group. These symptoms often affected children's daily activities and social development. The research also found no evidence of lasting heart problems in children, despite concerns about cardiac damage. The study emphasizes the need for coordinated care among different medical specialties due to the complexity of long-term symptoms. While most children recover completely, those who do not require further attention and support. The findings aim to help clinicians and families better understand and address the challenges faced by children with long COVID.

item.title: How Long Does Brain Fog Last After COVID-19? Study Offers Answers
item.description: A study published in the journal Neuroprotection investigated cognitive changes in 3,419 patients hospitalized with COVID-19 during the Omicron-dominant period in China, between December 2022 and March 2023. Researchers assessed cognitive function six months and two years post-infection, finding that 67.1% of participants maintained stable cognitive function, while 22.0% experienced reversible decline and 10.8% had irreversible decline. Age 60 years or older was linked to a more than fourfold higher risk of progressive decline, as were severe illness, hypertension, longer hospitalization, and white matter lesions. Higher education and more vaccination doses were protective factors. The study suggests that cognitive recovery is common after Omicron infection, but some patients may experience persistent deficits. These findings could help clinicians identify high-risk patients and guide targeted monitoring and rehabilitation strategies. Future studies with longer follow-up and in-person assessments are recommended to further understand cognitive recovery and progression.
